Tout

TOWT (rhymes with 'shout') -- from Middle English tuten ('to peer, look out'). · verb

Hear It

What It Means

To tout to aggressively promote or praise something, especially in order to sell it.

At the school fair, the sixth-grade club continually touted its bake-sale brownies as 'guaranteed to sell out by noon,' even on the two days they didn't.

Worked Example

The startup's CEO never stopped touting his app as 'the future of grocery shopping,' even to strangers waiting in line at the grocery store.

Notice tout is almost always about publicly, energetically talking something up -- a product, a plan, a candidate -- usually with an eye toward selling it or winning support, not quietly recommending it in private.

Antonyms

How Strong Is It? — promote → tout → hype

promote vs. tout

promote vs. tout: The city promoted the new bike-share program with flyers posted in every subway station.

hype vs. tout

hype vs. tout: Fans had hyped the sequel so much for two years that many were disappointed when it finally arrived.

Build the Word

The pieces

root — tout-

root — tout-: to peer, look out, keep watch (Middle English (tuten))

Put it together

Put it together: Tout began as a Middle English word for peering or looking out -- picture a lookout scanning the street for customers. That watching-for-buyers sense gradually shifted into today's meaning: loudly talking something up to attract attention and sales.

Use the root in a new word: touter

Use the root in a new word: touter: A racecourse touter used to make a living tipping off gamblers about which horse was supposedly guaranteed to win.
